$comment: The decision gate. Every question states what is already known, what is missing, and the cheapest action that would close it - so a decision can be made on information rather than instinct. 'answer' is left null wherever this session could not obtain it from an official source; those are not oversights, they are the gaps.
how_to_use: Answer inline (or on the Decisions page) top to bottom. A question with an answer moves the rows in its 'blocks' list from 'awaiting input' to 'decidable'.

sections.title: Inventory - what are we even promoting?
sections.why_first: Four of five product identities are inferred from a redirect, and none is confirmed by the owner. Every downstream choice - categories, clusters, keywords, comparison criteria - depends on this block.

questions.question: Are the four listings our short links currently resolve to the products you intend us to promote?
questions.known: link.amazon/B04G1MEwY -> amazon.com/dp/B0CDY277D3 'CHEFMAN 6 Quart Dual Basket Air Fryer Oven'; B02NbDxp3 -> B09B7SB46R 'Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door Multi-Function Air Fryer Toaster Oven'; B00hJ57DV -> B08DKYBTPH 'Chefman Air Fryer 8 Qt TurboFry 4-in-1'; B0f3GKalj -> B0DZFD6R9Z 'CHEF iQ Sense Smart Wireless Meat Thermometer'. Observed 2026-11-20.
questions.unknown: Whether that is owner intent or a redirect that drifted. Amazon short links can be retargeted; a token is not a stable identifier.
questions.how_to_close: Copy each ASIN out of Associates Central (Links > Special Links) and paste it into register/products.json:intended_asin.

questions.question: What is the product behind B0c8moW59? It did not resolve.
questions.known: Three fetch attempts returned an Amazon checkpoint interstitial. Nothing else is known.
questions.unknown: Brand, model, category, price band, even whether it is a kitchen product.
questions.how_to_close: Open the link in your own browser and paste the final URL. Or replace it.

questions.question: Is the thermometer a fourth air fryer in disguise, or a deliberate accessory attach?
questions.known: It resolved to CHEF iQ Sense, a wireless probe thermometer. The brief's editorial hypotheses are all air-fryer shaped.
questions.unknown: Whether the strategy is one category (air fryers) or two (air fryers + cooking instruments), which changes the site's topical authority plan and the cluster structure.
questions.how_to_close: One sentence from you: 'category = air fryers only' or 'category = air fryers + instruments'.

questions.question: Are there products beyond these five that should be in the first publish batch?
questions.known: Five links were supplied. The brief says 'test one link per product ... then scale', implying more are coming.
questions.unknown: The size and shape of the intended catalog, and therefore whether the site needs a real index/search now or later.
questions.how_to_close: Give a count and a category list, even approximate. The register already scales; the question is how much navigation to build now.

questions.question: Are any of these listings out of stock, discontinued, or region-restricted?
questions.known: Not determinable here. The listing bodies that would show it were not captured in a form we can stand behind.
questions.unknown: Availability - and a page promoting an unavailable product earns nothing and reads badly.
questions.how_to_close: Check each listing's Buy Box in a normal browser, or let the API do it once SG-13 is funded.

sections.title: Account and eligibility - can this legally earn?
sections.why_first: The whole model requires an approved Associates account with this site registered and this tracking ID live. Nothing on the site can be monetised until block B is green.

questions.question: Is tracking ID shopnow047c-20 actually created on the account?
questions.known: The brief states it as the selected tracking ID. Its format (-20 suffix, lowercase alphanumerics) is consistent with the convention.
questions.unknown: Existence, and whether it is attached to a registered site. Unverifiable without login.
questions.how_to_close: Associates Central > Account Settings > Tracking IDs. Screenshot the row; paste the URL into register/links.json.
blocks: every outbound link on the site

questions.question: Is the production domain registered as a Site on the account?
questions.known: The live site is currently a github.io subpath. Associates approval is per URL.
questions.unknown: Whether a custom domain is owned or intended, and whether the account is approved or still in the qualifying-sales window.
questions.how_to_close: Account Settings > Site Settings. Add the exact URL, including subpath.

questions.question: Are you inside the first-180-days qualifying-sales window, and does the account already have API access?
questions.known: New Associates accounts are expected to produce qualifying sales early or are closed and must re-apply - widely reported, and consistent with the Participation Requirements referenced by the Operating Agreement, which we could not fetch (S02).
questions.unknown: Your account age, sales count, API status, and the exact threshold. Reports > Earnings would answer all four.
questions.how_to_close: One look at Associates Central home page and Reports. Record the date and the numbers in register/ledger.json provenance.

questions.question: Which API should the pipeline target: PA-API 5.0 or the Creators API?
questions.known: Secondary sources report PA-API 5.0 being superseded by a Creators API with OAuth and re-registration. Sources conflict on the sales threshold (3 vs 10 qualifying sales in a trailing window). Official pages were unreachable in-session.
questions.unknown: The current official threshold and endpoint. Deliberately unresolved - see S07.
questions.how_to_close: Associates Central > Tools, look for the API access control, and read the eligibility sentence on screen. That one line resolves three rows.

questions.question: Do you accept that no prices appear on the site until API access exists?
questions.known: This session adopted strict suppression, and the build fails on any currency pattern. It costs the site some 'shop feel' and removes all stale-price risk.
questions.unknown: Whether you prefer the looser 'update manually and date-stamp it' approach used by most affiliate sites, which carries contract risk.
questions.how_to_close: Choose a path in SG-14. No further information needed - it is a preference about risk appetite.

sections.title: Editorial direction - what makes it a shop and not an audit
sections.why_first: The brief's central instruction is tone: buyer-facing, not compliance-facing. The register already exists as data; this block decides how the reading experience behaves.

questions.question: What is the shop's promise in one line?
questions.known: This build uses: 'we do not test, we tell you what to check'. It is honest, differentiated, and survives having no lab and no API. It also concedes the 'best X' search intents to competitors.
questions.unknown: Whether you want that positioning, or a conventional 'we tested the best' shop that this project cannot honestly produce today.
questions.how_to_close: Pick a path in SG-19. If you want tested reviews, the missing ingredient is physical product access - answer Q-12 with yes/no and we size that plan.

questions.question: Can anyone on your side buy or borrow the five products for real testing?
questions.known: No product is held by this project. Nothing that reads like a test result exists, and none was fabricated.
questions.unknown: Whether hands-on content is on the table at all, and at what unit cost.
questions.how_to_close: Yes/no plus a rough budget per product. If yes, the roadmap gains a 'protocol + photos + honest notes' track that is worth more than any on-page SEO tweak.

questions.question: Who signs off before a guide goes live - a named human, the desk byline, or nobody?
questions.known: Today: an automated pass plus a build gate, disclosed on the page as AI-assisted. A named byline with invented credentials is not an option this project will take.
questions.unknown: Whether a human editor exists, and whether you want their name on it. This is an E-E-A-T lever and a legal exposure question at the same time.
questions.how_to_close: Name a person and an email, or say 'keep the desk byline'. Then set the publish gate to require their approval or not.

questions.question: Which audience are we writing for - first-time buyer, upgrader, or household-scale shopper?
questions.known: The brief's hypotheses (capacity checklist, cleanup and counter space, multi-function questions) point at first and second-time buyers with small kitchens.
questions.unknown: Whether that is your commercial preference too, since it changes price band, tone and which products are worth adding.
questions.how_to_close: Pick one for the first six guides. Narrow beats accurate here.

questions.question: Seasonal angle for the next batch: back-to-school dorm kitchens, or holiday cooking?
questions.known: The brief lists 'seasons and clusters' as part of the reader-facing polish path. Today is 2026-11-20 - holiday cooking is live now, dorm kitchens is a January-August play.
questions.unknown: Whether you want to chase a live season with thin content or build the evergreen set first and schedule the season. This is a timing judgement, not a fact.
questions.how_to_close: Choose a path in SG-24.

questions.question: How much brand identity is already owned - name, logo, domain, social handles?
questions.known: This build derived the brand (ShopNow 047) from the supplied tracking ID 'shopnow047c-20' because the repo had no brand asset and no name. It is a placeholder with a rationale, not a decision by you.
questions.unknown: Whether you own or prefer a different name, and whether a domain is available.
questions.how_to_close: Say 'keep' or give the real brand string. One string changes the masthead, footer, feed title, and JSON-LD publisher.

sections.title: Measurement - what would tell us any of this worked
sections.why_first: The brief says measure before automating optimisation. Without these answers, the campaign ledger stays empty forever and every topic choice stays a guess.

questions.question: Is Search Console verified for the production domain?
questions.known: The brief's parallel pass SG-29 lists Search Console as a tracked row. This environment cannot verify a domain it does not own.
questions.unknown: Verification status, and therefore whether we can ever see the queries people actually arrive on.
questions.how_to_close: Add a DNS TXT record or HTML file at the production domain, verify, then export queries for the first 28 days.

questions.question: Where do you want click data to live, given the static host?
questions.known: GitHub Pages serves no backend. The click counter ships in two halves: a browser-side recorder with no cookies and no IP, and a 90-line Node collector that writes NDJSON and can run on any box you own.
questions.unknown: Whether you will run the collector, prefer a self-hosted analytics product (Plausible/Umami), or accept 'no click data at all' for launch.
questions.how_to_close: Choose a path in SG-27. Deploying the collector is a single command on a VPS.

questions.question: Do you have a privacy policy decision to make about analytics?
questions.known: The shipped counter uses no cookies, no fingerprinting, and no persistent identifier; the session id lives in sessionStorage and dies with the tab. That keeps it outside most consent regimes, but 'most' is not 'all' if you later target the EU.
questions.unknown: Whether the audience is US-only, and whether any consent tooling is wanted.
questions.how_to_close: Answer the jurisdiction question in SG-28. US-only means the current design stands as-is.

questions.question: What is the first success number, and by when?
questions.known: There is no baseline. Any target set now would be invented. The register defines what to count; it does not guess what 'good' is.
questions.unknown: Your tolerance: is '200 organic sessions in month two' a pass or a fail? Different answers change whether we invest in cadence or in one big pillar page.
questions.how_to_close: Set it after 28 days of Search Console data, not before. This question is on the list so it is not forgotten.

sections.title: Mechanics and money - what the pipeline may touch

questions.question: May the automation publish without a human in the loop?
questions.known: The brief asks for automation but also for 'a gate in front of the parts that cannot [be automated]'. Current build: fully automated generation, hard compliance gate at build time, no auto-publish to a monetised domain.
questions.unknown: Whether you want an overnight publish job on the live domain once the site is approved - which changes the risk profile of a bad row.
questions.how_to_close: Choose a path in SG-31 (gate at commit vs gate at publish vs no gate).

questions.question: What is the monthly budget for data and hosting?
questions.known: Everything shipped here runs on free tiers: GitHub Pages, stdlib Node, no npm dependencies, no paid data.
questions.unknown: Whether a domain, a VPS for the collector, or an SEO dataset is in budget. That determines if SG-13, SG-20 and SG-32 are live options or paper options.
questions.how_to_close: A number, even a range. Below 20/month the current build is the right build.

numbering_note: IDs Q-01..Q-22 are contiguous. Nothing was dropped from this register; two rows that an earlier outline contemplated (search-volume and paid-traffic targets) were never created, because no source for either exists in this repository and an invented figure would have looked like a measurement.
